chapters.title: Introduction: All Things Are Not What They Seem

assets.topic: Reading All Things Are Not What They Seem
assets.visual_frame_description: A Victorian gentleman being scrutinized by Sherlock Holmes through a magnifying glass, with annotations highlighting fingernails, coat-sleeve, boots, and trouser-knees. Each body part reveals a clue about his occupation, habits, and character.

assets.visual_frame_description: A conference table with different seating positions highlighted in color codes: corner position (cooperative), cooperative side-by-side, competitive face-to-face, independent far-end. Each position triggers a popup explaining the strategic advantage.
assets.player_mission: Analyze 15 meeting room setups and identify the strategic implications of each seating arrangement. Determine who has positional advantage, who is isolated, and which positions foster cooperation vs. competition.
key_concepts: Corner seating at a 90-degree angle fosters cooperation and casual conversation
Face-to-face seating creates a competitive or defensive atmosphere
Side-by-side seating signals alliance and shared purpose
The left side of a table is often where the most attentive people sit
